items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the eligibility of independent institutions of higher education to receive assistance from the New York power authority in establishing energy efficiency and clean energy initiatives
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S3755

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the eligibility of
independent institutions of higher education to receive assistance from
the New York power authority in establishing energy efficiency and clean
energy initiatives

PURPOSE:
To allow independent Colleges and Universities to access
programs administered by the New York Power Authority that relate to
energy efficiency and clean energy.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:
Section 1 Amends paragraph (a) of subdivision 16 of section 1005 of
the public authorities law, as added by chapter 477 of the laws of
2009 to add independent not-for-profit institutions of higher
education to the list of entities eligible for assistance from the
New York Power Authority for energy related projects.

JUSTIFICATION:
Existing law allows the New York Power Authority to
design, develop, finance construct, implement or provide and
administer energy related projects, programs and services for public
entities and for recipients of power allocations under the
Authorities various low-cost power programs. The stated purpose of
the bill that authorized this program in 2009 was to enhance the
energy efficiency, clean energy, energy service and green building
programs administered by the Power Authority of the State of New York
(NYPA), to reduce energy consumption and mitigate environmental
impacts from energy usage consistent with the State's energy and
environmental policies. To that end, the inclusion of independent
Colleges and Universities will merely enhance the laudable goals of
the original legislation and further promote a cleaner environment
while reducing energy usage. At the same time, this bill would assist
independent Colleges and Universities in reducing their energy costs,
and could have a positive impact on tuition and other fees that are
necessary for their operations.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately, with provisions.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the eligibility of independent not-for-profit institutions of higher education to access energy-related projects, programs and services of the New York power authority and the meaning of energy-related projects, programs and services
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S3755A

TITLE OF BILL:

An act
to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the eligibility of
independent not-for-profit
institutions of higher education to
access energy-related projects, programs and services of
the New York power authority
and the meaning of energy-related projects, programs and services

PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to allow independent not-for-profit
colleges and universities to access energy-related projects, programs
and services of the New York Power Authority ("NYPA"), and to expand
the scope of NYPA's "energy-related projects, programs and services."

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill would amend Public Authorities Law
§1005(16)(a), as added by Chapter 477 of the Laws of 2009, to add
independent not-for-profit institutions of higher education to the
list of entities that are eligible to access the energy-related
projects, programs and services of NYPA.

Section 2 of this bill would amend Public Authorities Law
§1005(16)(b)(2) and (4) to: (1) add "research, development and
demonstration of new systems, technologies and materials relating to
energy usage, storage, transmission and efficiency" to the definition
of "energy-related projects, programs and services;" and (2) clarify
that "high performance and sustainable building programs and
services" includes programs and services related to construction, in
addition to renovation and retrofitting, of buildings, and that such
programs and services may be addressed to the use of clean energy and
fuels in addition to renewable energy.

Section 3 of this bill would provide for the bill's effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

Public Authorities Law § 1005(16) authorizes NYPA to design, develop,
finance construct, implement or provide and administer energy related
projects, programs and services for public entities and for
recipients of various NYPA power allocation programs. The purpose of
this provision is to enhance the energy efficiency, clean energy,
energy service and green building
programs administered by NYPA, to reduce energy consumption and
mitigate environmental impacts from energy usage consistent with the
State's energy and environmental policies.

Authorizing independent not-for-profit colleges and universities to
access NYPA's energy related projects, programs and services, and
expanding the definition of "energy-related projects, programs and
services" would further these laudable goals. In addition, providing
these colleges and universities with access to NYPA's programs and
services could help such institutions reduce their energy costs which
in turn could have favorable impacts on tuition and fees.

Expanding NYPA's "energy-related projects, programs and services" to
include "research, development and demonstration of new systems,
technologies and materials relating to energy usage, storage,
transmission and efficiency," would also provide a basis to help the
State's colleges and universities remain competitive in these subject
areas, and could help stimulate vital partnerships and other joint
endeavors between the State, the State's businesses and these
institutions. The marriage of these interests could lead to
significant new "Made in New York" innovations in the energy field
which in turn would support the State's energy and environmental
policies as well as support economic development in New York.

Finally, the amendments to Public Authorities Law § 1005(16)(b)(2) and
(4) would clarify that NYPA's high performance and sustainable
building programs and services may relate to construction, in
addition to renovation and retrofitting, of buildings, and that such
programs and services may be addressed to clean energy sources and
fuels (e.g., hydrogen) in addition to renewable energy sources such
as wind and solar. As we continue to face significant challenges in
the energy field, including the need for more energy and the
consequences of increased energy usage, we cannot afford to limit our
consideration of possible solutions to accepted or established
technologies.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This bill would take effect immediately; provided, however, the
amendments to subdivision 16 of section 1005 of the Public Authorities
Law made by sections one and two of the bill would not affect the
expiration of such subdivision and would expire therewith.

Authorizing independent not-for-profit colleges and universities to

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This bill would take effect immediately.
